claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy.
The feedstock particle-size distribution is 15–45 μm.
The feedstock has a typical gas-atomized microstructure.
Standard HVAF-i7 deposition of the 15–45 μm feedstock previously produced acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
The proposed intervention combines a 300–350 mm stand-off distance with modified shielding-gas and oxygen–fuel settings.
Increasing the spray distance to 300–350 mm accelerates particles to higher velocities.
Higher particle velocity improves in-flight deformation, flattening, and interparticle or substrate bonding.
Higher particle kinetic energy enhances deposition efficiency.
Improved impact momentum and splat formation will produce a thicker coating.
High-velocity combustion spraying can produce thick coatings with low porosity and high adhesion.
Adjusting the shielding environment and oxygen–fuel ratio will reduce in-flight oxidation.
The tailored gas environment will reduce porosity formation.
The combined intervention will yield a significantly thicker and more adherent coating than standard HVAF-i7 processing.
The combined intervention will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
The resulting coating will be suitable for high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention is applicable to substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Longer oxygen exposure during flight can increase particle oxidation, particularly for smaller particles.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy may introduce increased porosity.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that increasing spray distance accelerates particles and raises impact kinetic energy, whereas the cited conflicting record reports that longer spray distance lowers impact kinetic energy, slightly decreases coating thickness, and increases porosity.

The predicted outcome attributes greater thickness and minimal oxidation to the longer stand-off distance, while the cited conflicting evidence reports slightly lower thickness and greater oxide content as spray distance increases.
